questions.question: The Peninsular rivers that flow into the Arabian Sea are:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narmada, Tapi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Narmada** and **Tapi** are the two major **west-flowing** rivers of the **Peninsular Plateau** that empty into the **Arabian Sea**.
 
• The **Narmada River** originates from the **Amarkantak** hill range in **Madhya Pradesh**. It flows through a **rift valley** formed by **faulting** between the **Vindhya** and **Satpura** ranges, covering a distance of about 1,312 km.
 
• The **Tapi River**, also known as the **Tapti**, originates in the **Satpura** ranges in the **Betul** district of **Madhya Pradesh**. It flows parallel to the Narmada in a **rift valley** for approximately 724 km.
 
• Unlike the east-flowing rivers that form extensive **deltas**, the Narmada and Tapi form **estuaries** at their mouths in the **Gulf of Khambhat** due to the high gradient and the hard rocky terrain they traverse.
 
• The westward flow of these rivers is an exception to the general **eastward tilt** of the **Deccan Plateau**, caused by the geological **subsidence** of the land during the **Himalayan** mountain-building process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **East-flowing Peninsular Rivers**:

 
 
• **Godavari**: Known as the **Dakshin Ganga**, it is the longest peninsular river and flows into the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• **Krishna**: Originates near **Mahabaleshwar** and forms a large delta on the east coast before entering the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• **Mahanadi**: Drains the state of **Chhattisgarh** and **Odisha**, emptying into the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• **Kaveri**: A sacred river of south India that originates in the **Brahmagiri** hills and flows eastwards.
 
 
 
• **Specific River Characteristics**:
 
 
• **Periyar**: This is a major **west-flowing** river in **Kerala**, but it is often excluded from the primary list of major peninsular rivers like Narmada and Tapi in standard classifications.
 
• **Subarnarekha**: An east-flowing river that passes through the **Chhota Nagpur Plateau** and reaches the **Bay of Bengal**.

questions.question: Which regional power rose to prominence in northern India after the decline of the Gupta Empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pushyabhutis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pushyabhuti Dynasty**, also famously known as the **Vardhana Dynasty**, rose to prominence in **Northern India** during the late 6th and early 7th centuries CE, following the fragmentation of the **Gupta Empire**.
 
• The dynasty was established in **Sthanishvara** (modern-day **Thanesar** in Haryana) and eventually filled the political vacuum created by the decline of the **Imperial Guptas** and the subsequent invasions of the **Hunas**.
 
• The most illustrious ruler of this dynasty was **Harshavardhana** (606−647 CE), who succeeded in uniting several small regional principalities to form a vast empire that spanned across the **Indo-Gangetic plains**.
 
• Under **Harshavardhana**, the capital was shifted from **Thanesar** to **Kannauj**, establishing it as the premier political and cultural center of **North India** for several centuries.
 
• The **Pushyabhutis** maintained a highly centralized administration initially but later transitioned toward a more feudal structure, which became a defining characteristic of the **Post-Gupta** political landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regional Context of Other Options:**

 
 
• The **Cholas** and **Cheras** were powerful dynasties of **Southern India** (Tamil Nadu and Kerala regions) and had no direct role in the immediate power transition in **Northern India** post-Gupta decline.
 
• The **Vakatakas** were a major power in the **Deccan** (Central India) and were contemporaries of the **Guptas**, linked via marriage alliances, but their influence also faded by the early 6th century.
 
 
 
• **Primary Historical Sources:**
 
 
• Detailed accounts of the **Pushyabhuti** era are found in the **Harshacharita**, a biography written by the court poet **Banabhatta**, and the travelogues of the Chinese monk **Xuanzang** (Hiuen Tsang).
 
 
 
• **Administrative Features:**
 
 
• The **Vardhana** administration involved a hierarchy of officials such as the **Mahasandhivigrahaka** (Minister for War and Peace) and **Rajasthaniya** (Viceroys), which stabilized the region after decades of instability.

questions.question: The decline in the Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) in India can be primarily attributed to which of the following factors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All of these**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Better neonatal care** has been a cornerstone in reducing infant deaths, particularly through the establishment of **Special Newborn Care Units (SNCUs)** and **Newborn Stabilization Units (NBSUs)** that provide emergency care for complications like **birth asphyxia** and **pre-term birth**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **Expansion of immunization programs**, such as the **Universal Immunization Programme (UIP)** and **Mission Indradhanush**, has drastically lowered the incidence of **vaccine-preventable diseases** like **measles**, **tetanus**, and **whooping cough** among infants. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Improved maternal health** ensures better birth outcomes; initiatives like **Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)** and **Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK)** promote **institutional deliveries** and provide **antenatal care**, reducing **neonatal mortality**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)**:

 
 
• It is defined as the number of deaths of children under **one year** of age per **1,000 live births**.
 
• According to **Sample Registration System (SRS)** data, India has seen a steady decline in IMR from **37** in 2015 to approximately **28** in 2020.
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG)** target for India is to reduce the IMR to **25** or less by the year **2030**.
 
 
 
• **Supplementary Programs**:
 
 
• **POSHAN Abhiyaan**: Aimed at improving the nutritional status of children and **pregnant women** to prevent **low birth weight**.
 
• **Home Based Newborn Care (HBNC)**: Empowers **ASHA workers** to conduct home visits and identify **danger signs** in newborns early.
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY)**: Provides **direct benefit transfers** to pregnant women to compensate for wage loss and ensure adequate **nutrition**.

questions.question: Which act provided the legal basis for the creation of Pakistan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Independence Act, 1947**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Independence Act, 1947** was an act of the **Parliament of the United Kingdom** that received **Royal Assent** on **July 18, 1947**.
 
• It provided the **statutory authority** for the partition of **British India** and the establishment of two independent dominions: **India** and **Pakistan**.
 
• The act mandated the cessation of **British Suzerainty** over the **Princely States** and the lapse of all treaties with them, effective from **August 15, 1947**.
 
• It provided for the creation of **Pakistan** comprising the territories of **East Bengal**, **West Punjab**, **Sindh**, and the **North-West Frontier Province (NWFP)**.
 
• The legislation empowered the **Constituent Assemblies** of both nations to frame and adopt their own constitutions and to repeal any British law, including the Independence Act itself.
 
• It designated the **Radcliffe Commission** to determine the international boundaries between the two newly formed nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)**:

 
 
• Proposed a **united India** with a three-tier administrative structure to address the **Muslim League’s** demand for autonomy without partition.
 
• It failed as the **Indian National Congress** and the **Muslim League** could not agree on the interpretation of the **grouping clause**.
 
 
 
• **Mountbatten Plan (June 3, 1947)**:
 
 
• Also known as the **Partition Plan**, it was the political framework that accepted the **Two-Nation Theory**.
 
• It proposed an earlier date for the transfer of power and introduced **referendums** in **Sylhet** and **NWFP**.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1935**:
 
 
• The longest act of the British Parliament, it introduced **Provincial Autonomy** and a **Federal Court**.
 
• It served as the **interim constitution** for both India and Pakistan until 1950 and 1956, respectively.

questions.question: What mission to tackle illegal immigration was announced on Independence Day 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Demography Mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the **79th Independence Day** address from the **Red Fort** on **August 15, 2025**, the Prime Minister announced the launch of the **Demography Mission** to address the complex challenges posed by **illegal immigration** and shifting population patterns.
 
• The mission is designed as a strategic response to maintain the **socio-cultural balance** and **internal security** of the nation, particularly in sensitive regions where demographic changes have been most pronounced.
 
• The **Demography Mission** aims to implement rigorous **biometric identification** systems and digital tracking to identify individuals staying in the country without valid authorization.
 
• It involves a multi-agency approach, led by the **Ministry of Home Affairs**, to strengthen **border surveillance** and prevent the unauthorized crossing of international boundaries.
 
• The initiative also focuses on protecting the **rights and resources** of **indigenous communities** and legal citizens by ensuring that government benefits and citizenship privileges are not misappropriated by illegal residents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Illegal Immigration in India**:

 
 
• Governed primarily by the **Foreigners Act, 1946**, which empowers the central government to regulate the entry, presence, and departure of foreigners.
 
• The **Passport (Entry into India) Act, 1920**, also mandates that all persons entering the country must possess valid travel documents.
 
• The issue is particularly significant in the **Northeastern states** and **West Bengal**, where long, porous borders share proximity with neighboring countries.
 
 
 
• **Viksit Bharat 2047**:
 
 
• The **Demography Mission** aligns with the broader goal of **Viksit Bharat** (Developed India) by **2047**, ensuring that national development is not hindered by **security vulnerabilities** or unmonitored population growth.
 
• The 2025 address emphasized **national unity** and the importance of a transparent **National Register** for effective governance and security management.

questions.question: In _____, the Government of India set up a committee under the chairmanship of RN Malhotra, former Governor of RBI, to propose recommendations for reforms in the insurance sector.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1993**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India** officially set up the **Committee on Reforms in the Insurance Sector** in **1993** to evaluate the existing structure and suggest improvements to the industry.
 
• The committee was led by **R.N. Malhotra**, who served as the **Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** from 1985 to 1990, ensuring a high level of financial expertise in the reform process.
 
• The primary objective of the **Malhotra Committee** was to complement the **New Economic Policy** of 1991 by introducing **liberalization** and **competition** into a sector that was previously a state monopoly.
 
• The committee submitted its landmark report in **January 1994**, advocating for the entry of **private sector players** and permitting **foreign promoters** to hold a stake in Indian insurance companies.
 
• Its recommendations focused on increasing the **insurance penetration** and **density** in India, which were significantly lower than global averages at that time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legislative and Regulatory Outcomes**

 
 
• Following the committee's report, the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDA) Act** was passed in **1999**.
 
• This led to the creation of the **IRDAI** in **April 2000**, a statutory body tasked with regulating and promoting the **insurance and re-insurance** industries.
 
• The opening of the sector ended the monopoly of the **Life Insurance Corporation (LIC)** and **General Insurance Corporation (GIC)**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context of Nationalization**
 
 
• The **Life Insurance** business was nationalized in **1956**, merging 245 Indian and foreign providers into the **LIC**.
 
• The **General Insurance** business was nationalized via the **General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1972**, effective from January 1, 1973.
 
• The **Malhotra Committee** suggested that the **Government of India** should reduce its stake in these public sector entities to **50 percent** to allow more autonomy.

questions.question:
Which of the following is NOT a pillar of DAJA Abhiyan?

I. Job security

II. Cultural Inclusion
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Job security** typically refers to the protection of formal employment in organized sectors. While the **DAJA Abhiyan** (Dignity and Justice Action) emphasizes **Livelihood Security** and the restoration of **Land Rights** for traditional occupations, formal 'job security' is not designated as a specific pillar of this grassroots movement. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Cultural Inclusion** is a foundational pillar of the **DAJA Abhiyan**. It focuses on removing the **social stigma** and the 'criminal' label historically attached to certain tribes, ensuring their **social dignity**, and promoting the preservation of their unique **cultural heritage** and **languages**. ***Hence, statement II is incorrect.***
 
• The **DAJA Abhiyan** is a rights-based movement primarily working for the empowerment and **social justice** of the **De-notified, Nomadic, and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs)** in India, focusing on pillars like **Identity**, **Education**, **Health**, and **Political Participation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **De-notified Tribes** were formerly notified as 'born criminals' under the **Criminal Tribes Act of 1871** during British rule.

 
 
• This discriminatory act was repealed on **August 31, 1952**, a day now celebrated by these communities as **Vimukta Diwas** (Liberation Day).
 
• Despite the repeal, the subsequent **Habitual Offenders Act** continued to facilitate the **social marginalization** of these groups.
 
• The **Idate Commission** and the **Renke Commission** are significant bodies established by the **Government of India** to study the socio-economic status of **DNTs** and recommend welfare measures.
 
• Key demands of movements like **DAJA** include the issuance of **Caste Certificates**, implementation of **Social Security** schemes, and protection against **police harassment**.

questions.question: 'Dashavatara' is a folk dance of which of the following Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dashavatara** is a highly stylized traditional folk theatre and dance-drama practiced in the **Konkan** region, primarily in **Goa** and the **Sindhudurg** district of **Maharashtra**.
 
• The performance is dedicated to the ten incarnations of **Lord Vishnu**, known as the **Dashavatara**: **Matsya**, **Kurma**, **Varaha**, **Narasimha**, **Vamana**, **Parashurama**, **Rama**, **Krishna**, **Buddha**, and **Kalki**.
 
• The art form is traditionally showcased during **Jatras** (annual temple festivals) and religious ceremonies, acting as a vital link between the community and **Hindu mythology**.
 
• The performance structure includes the **Purvaranga** (the initial invocation of **Lord Ganesha**) and the **Uttararanga** (the main mythological narrative or play).
 
• Performers, historically all male, utilize **vibrant wooden masks**, elaborate makeup, and traditional costumes, accompanied by live music featuring the **Harmonium**, **Tabla**, and **Zanj**.
 
• The lead narrator, known as the **Sutradhar**, orchestrates the performance, blending rhythmic prose with poetic verses to guide the audience through the epic stories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goa**:

 
 
• **Fugdi** and **Dhalo** are prominent folk dances performed by women during festivals like **Ganesh Chaturthi**.
 
• The **Kunbi** dance is a rhythmic folk form performed by the indigenous **Kunbi** community of the state.
 
 
 
• **Chhattisgarh**:
 
 
• **Pandavani** is a famous folk ballad that narrates episodes from the **Mahabharata**, popularized by artists like **Teejan Bai**.
 
• The **Panthi** dance is a spiritual performance of the **Satnami** community, while **Raut Nacha** is performed by cowherds.
 
 
 
• **Haryana**:
 
 
• **Phag** is a seasonal dance performed by farmers during the month of **Phalgun**.
 
• The **Dhamal** dance is an ancient form dating back to the **Mahabharata**, performed on moonlit nights.
 
 
 
• **Himachal Pradesh**:
 
 
• **Nati** is the most famous folk dance, often performed during local fairs and the **Kullu Dussehra**.
 
• **Chham** is a masked ritual dance performed by Buddhist monks (Lamas) in monasteries.

questions.question: Which cyclone affected Odisha and West Bengal in October 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cyclone Dana** was a severe cyclonic storm that formed in the **Bay of Bengal** in **October 2024**, specifically making landfall during the late hours of **October 24** and early hours of **October 25**.
 
• The storm made landfall on the **Odisha coast** between **Bhitarkanika National Park** and **Dhamra Port** in the **Bhadrak** district, with wind speeds ranging from **100 to 110 kmph**, gusting up to **120 kmph**.
 
• The name **Dana** was proposed by **Qatar**, which translates to a 'generous' or 'perfectly sized, valuable, and beautiful pearl' in **Arabic**.
 
• The state governments of **Odisha** and **West Bengal** evacuated over **600,000** and **200,000** people respectively to **cyclone shelters** to minimize casualties before the storm struck.
 
• The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** monitored the system as it moved northwestwards, bringing heavy to extremely heavy rainfall to coastal districts like **Kendrapara**, **Balasore**, and **East Medinipur**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Recent Cyclones**:

 
 
• **Cyclone Yaas**: A **Very Severe Cyclonic Storm** that hit the **Odisha** and **West Bengal** coasts in **May 2021**, causing significant storm surges in the **Sundarbans**.
 
• **Cyclone Gulab**: Affected the coasts of **Andhra Pradesh** and **Odisha** in **September 2021**. It was named by **Pakistan**.
 
• **Cyclone Shaheen**: Formed in the **Arabian Sea** in **October 2021** from the remnants of **Cyclone Gulab**; it eventually impacted **Oman**.
 
 
 
• **Naming Authority**: Tropical cyclones in the **North Indian Ocean** are named by the **IMD** and 12 other member countries of the **WMO/ESCAP** Panel on Tropical Cyclones to avoid confusion during **disaster management** operations.

questions.question: In which Indian city is the 'Harballabh Sangeet Mela' celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jalandhar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Harballabh Sangeet Mela** is held annually at the sacred **Devi Talab Mandir** located in **Jalandhar**, **Punjab**.
 
• It is globally recognized as the **oldest festival** of **Indian Classical Music** in the world, having been celebrated continuously since its inception in **1875**.
 
• The festival was founded by **Baba Harballabh**, a saint and a great devotee of **Indian Classical Music**, to honor his guru, **Swami Tulja Giri**.
 
• The event typically takes place during the last week of **December** and serves as a major pilgrimage for students and exponents of **Hindustani Classical Music**.
 
• In recognition of its immense cultural and historical value, the **Government of India** has officially designated the mela as a **National Festival**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gwalior**:

 
 
• Famous for the **Tansen Samaroh** (Tansen Music Festival), which is held near the tomb of the legendary musician **Tansen** at **Behat**.
 
• It is a major center for the **Gwalior Gharana**, one of the oldest **Khayal** gharanas of Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Varanasi**:
 
 
• Known for the **Sankat Mochan Sangeet Samaroh**, an annual festival of classical music and dance held at the **Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple**.
 
• It is also famous for the **Dhrupad Mela** held at **Tulsi Ghat**, focusing on the ancient **Dhrupad** style.
 
 
 
• **Shree Baba Harballabh Sangeet Mahasabha**:
 
 
• This is the dedicated body that organizes the **Harballabh Sangeet Mela** and works toward the preservation and promotion of **classical music** traditions.

questions.question: What happens to the kinetic energy of particles as the temperature of the matter increases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Temperature** is fundamentally defined as a measure of the **average kinetic energy** of the particles within a substance.
 
• According to the **Kinetic Molecular Theory**, all matter is composed of tiny particles (atoms or molecules) that are in **constant, random motion**.
 
• When the temperature of matter is raised, **thermal energy** is transferred to the particles, which causes them to **move faster** in gases and liquids or **vibrate more intensely** in solids.
 
• The formula for kinetic energy is **1/2 mv²**, where **m** represents mass and **v** represents velocity; therefore, as the **velocity** of the particles increases with heat, their **kinetic energy** also rises proportionally.
 
• At higher temperatures, the **frequency of collisions** between particles increases because they possess more energy to overcome **intermolecular forces**.
 
• This relationship is direct; specifically, for an **ideal gas**, the average translational kinetic energy is **directly proportional** to the **absolute temperature** (measured in Kelvin).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Absolute Zero**:

 
 
• This occurs at **0 Kelvin** (−273.15 degrees Celsius), the point where **particle motion** reaches its theoretical minimum and kinetic energy is effectively **zero**.
 
 
 
• **States of Matter and Energy**:
 
 
• **Gases**: Particles have the highest kinetic energy, allowing them to move independently and fill any container.
 
• **Liquids**: Particles have sufficient kinetic energy to slide past each other but remain bound by **attractive forces**.
 
• **Solids**: Particles have the lowest kinetic energy, restricted to **vibrational motion** around fixed positions in a **lattice structure**.
 
 
 
• **Potential Energy vs. Kinetic Energy**:
 
 
• While **kinetic energy** relates to motion, **potential energy** in matter is associated with the **bonds and forces** between particles. During **phase changes** (like melting ice), temperature remains constant because the added energy increases **potential energy** rather than kinetic energy.

questions.question: When tax collection exceeds the required expenditure, the budget is said to be ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**surplus budget**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **surplus budget** is a financial state where the **total estimated receipts** (revenue) of the government exceed the **total estimated expenditure** in a given financial year.
 
• The primary source of this revenue is **tax collection**, including both **direct taxes** (like income tax) and **indirect taxes** (like GST), along with non-tax revenues such as **dividends** from public enterprises and **interest receipts**.
 
• Mathematically, it is represented as **Total Revenue > Total Expenditure**. This indicates that the government is earning more than it is spending on public services, infrastructure, and administration.
 
• In economic terms, a surplus budget acts as a **contractionary fiscal policy** tool. By keeping more money in the treasury and reducing the **money supply** in the market, it helps to curb **inflation** during an overheated economy.
 
• A surplus allows a nation to reduce its **national debt** or save for future **contingencies**, often signifying a high level of **fiscal discipline** or a period of robust **economic growth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deficit Budget**:

 
 
• Occurs when the government **expenditure** exceeds its **revenue** (Expenditure > Revenue).
 
• Commonly used during **economic recessions** to boost **aggregate demand** and stimulate growth through increased public spending.
 
 
 
• **Balanced Budget**:
 
 
• A situation where the government's **total expenditure** is exactly equal to its **total receipts**.
 
• It signifies a neutral fiscal stance, ensuring **financial stability** without increasing debt or accumulating reserves.
 
 
 
• **Zero Budgeting**:
 
 
• Technically referred to as **Zero-Based Budgeting (ZBB)**, it is a method where every expense must be **justified** for each new period.
 
• Unlike traditional budgeting, it starts from a **zero base**, ignoring previous year allocations to eliminate **wasteful spending**.

questions.question: With respect to mineral resources in India, what does "CBM" mainly stand for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coal Bed Methane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coal Bed Methane (CBM)** is a form of **natural gas** extracted from coal beds or coal seams, where it is held by a process known as **adsorption**.
 
• It is classified as an **unconventional energy resource** because the gas is stored within the rock (coal) itself rather than in the pore spaces of traditional reservoir rocks like sandstone.
 
• India has significant potential for CBM production due to its massive **Gondwana coal reserves**, which are primarily located in the eastern and central parts of the country.
 
• The **Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH)** under the **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas** regulates and monitors the exploration and commercial production of CBM in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical Distribution in India:**

 
 
• Significant CBM blocks are identified in states like **Jharkhand**, **West Bengal**, **Chhattisgarh**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and **Rajasthan**.
 
• The **Raniganj** coalfield in West Bengal and the **Jharia** coalfield in Jharkhand are among the most prominent areas for CBM activity.
 
 
 
• **Composition and Extraction:**
 
 
• CBM is composed primarily of **Methane (CH₄)**, typically exceeding 90 percent purity, making it a **clean-burning fuel**.
 
• Extraction involves drilling a well into the coal seam and pumping out **formation water** to reduce the hydrostatic pressure, which triggers the release of the gas.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Safety Benefits:**
 
 
• Utilizing CBM reduces the risk of **explosions** in underground coal mines by pre-draining the gas before mining begins.
 
• It serves as an important feedstock for **fertilizer plants**, **power generation**, and as **Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)** for the transport sector.

questions.question:
Which of the following was a host city of the National Games 1994?

__
 
• The **31st National Games** of India were held in the year **1994** in the state of **Maharashtra**. Hence, statement I is correct.
 
• The games were jointly hosted by two major cities, **Bombay** (now **Mumbai**) and **Pune**, to accommodate the vast number of sporting disciplines and athletes. Hence, statement II is correct.
 
• The **1994 National Games** are noted for modernizing sports infrastructure in **Maharashtra**, leading to the development of world-class facilities in both **Bombay** and **Pune**.

• The National Games comprise various disciplines in which sportsmen from the different states of **India** participate against each other.
 
• The first edition of the **Indian Olympic Games** (the precursor to the National Games) was held in **1924** in **Lahore**, undivided **India**.

questions.question: What was the share of India's services exports in 1993 in world services?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.5%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the year **1993**, India's share in **world services exports** was recorded at **0.5%**, reflecting its marginal presence in the global trade arena at that time.
 
• This period immediately followed the **1991 Economic Reforms**, which introduced **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)** to the Indian economy, gradually opening up the **services sector** to international competition.
 
• During the early 1990s, India's service basket was dominated by **traditional services** such as **shipping**, **transportation**, and **travel**, while modern services like **Information Technology (IT)** were still in a nascent developmental phase.
 
• The global services market in **1993** was primarily controlled by developed economies, specifically the **European Union** and the **United States**, with developing nations having limited market penetration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Evolution of **India's Services Exports**:

 
 
• Post-1993, the sector witnessed exponential growth due to the **Y2K boom** and the subsequent rise of **Software Technology Parks of India (STPI)**.
 
• By **2000-2001**, India's share in global services doubled as the **IT-BPM (Information Technology - Business Process Management)** sector began to mature.
 
• According to the **World Trade Organization (WTO)** and the **Economic Survey of India**, India's share in world commercial services exports rose to approximately **4.4%** by **2022**, making it one of the largest exporters of services globally.
 
• The **Service Sector** is now a critical driver of the **Indian Economy**, contributing over **50%** to the national **Gross Value Added (GVA)** and attracting significant **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**.
 
• Current exports are driven by high-value segments like **Global Capability Centers (GCCs)**, **professional management consultancy**, and **digitally delivered services**.

questions.question: In Tennis, if both players win three points each in a game (i.e score is 40-40), then it's called a ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**deuce**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sport of **Tennis**, the standard scoring system for a single game progresses from **Love (0)** to **15 (1 point)**, **30 (2 points)**, and **40 (3 points)**.
 
• When both players or doubles teams reach a score of **40-40**, meaning each has won three points, the situation is known as a **deuce**.
 
• Once a game reaches **deuce**, a player must win two consecutive points to claim the game. The first point won after a deuce is called **Advantage**.
 
• If the player with the **Advantage** wins the subsequent point, they win the game; however, if they lose that point, the score returns to **deuce**.
 
• This rule ensures that a game cannot be won by a margin of only one point once the score is tied at the highest level of **standard play**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Love**:

 
 
• This term is used in tennis to denote a **score of zero** for a player or team in a game or set.
 
• Etymologically, it is widely believed to come from the French word **l'oeuf**, which means **the egg**, representing the circular shape of a zero.
 
 
 
• **Slice**:
 
 
• A **slice** is a type of shot where the player strikes the ball with an open racket face to produce **backspin**.
 
• This technique causes the ball to travel with a lower trajectory and **skid** or stay low upon hitting the court surface, making it difficult for the opponent to return.
 
 
 
• **Smash**:
 
 
• A **smash** (or overhead) is a high-velocity shot hit above the player's head with a motion similar to a **serve**.
 
• It is typically an aggressive response to a **lob** and is often used as a finishing move to win a point.

questions.question: "RESIDEX" Index in India is related to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Housing Price**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **RESIDEX** is India's first official **Housing Price Index (HPI)**, formulated to track the movement of prices in the **residential real estate** segment across the country. Hence, the link to housing price is correct.
 
• It was launched in **July 2007** by the **National Housing Bank (NHB)**, which serves as the apex regulatory body for **housing finance companies** in India. Hence, the regulatory origin is established.
 
• The index was initially developed with **2007** as the base year to provide **transparency** and a **standardized benchmark** for stakeholders such as **lenders**, **property developers**, and **homebuyers**. Hence, its functional role is to monitor property value fluctuations.
 
• Since **April 2017**, the NHB revamped the **RESIDEX** by shifting the base year to **2017-18** and expanding its scope to cover **50 cities**, categorizing indices into **HPI @ Assessment Prices** and **HPI @ Market Prices**. Hence, its methodology remains centered on urban housing costs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stock Market Performance**:

 
 
• This is measured by indices such as the **S&P BSE SENSEX** and the **NIFTY 50**, which track the market capitalization of listed companies on the **Bombay Stock Exchange** and **National Stock Exchange**.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Production**:
 
 
• This is tracked via the **Index of Industrial Production (IIP)**, compiled monthly by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** to measure the growth of various sectors like **mining**, **manufacturing**, and **electricity**.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Commodity**:
 
 
• Prices and performance in this sector are monitored through the **Wholesale Price Index (WPI)** and platforms like **e-NAM** (National Agriculture Market).

questions.question: The Global Terrorism Index is issued by Institute for Economics and Peace based in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Australia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP)** is an independent, non-partisan, and non-profit international think tank headquartered in **Sydney**, **Australia**.
 
• Founded in **2007** by IT entrepreneur and philanthropist **Steve Killelea**, the institute aims to shift the world’s focus to peace as a positive, achievable, and tangible measure of human well-being and progress.
 
• The **Global Terrorism Index (GTI)** is an annual report published by the **IEP** that provides a comprehensive summary of the key global trends and patterns in terrorism over the last decade.
 
• The index analyzes the impact of terrorism in **163 countries**, which covers **99.7%** of the world’s population, using data from the **Global Terrorism Database (GTD)** and other reputable sources.
 
• Countries are scored on a scale from **0 to 10**, where **0** represents no impact from terrorism and **10** represents the highest measurable impact, based on four indicators: **total incidents**, **fatalities**, **injuries**, and **property damage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Peace Index (GPI)**:

 
 
• Also produced by the **IEP**, this index is the world’s leading measure of global peacefulness, ranking countries according to their levels of **societal safety**, **domestic conflict**, and **militarization**.
 
 
 
• **Positive Peace Index**:
 
 
• This framework measures the **attitudes, institutions, and structures** that create and sustain peaceful societies, such as **low levels of corruption** and **high levels of human capital**.
 
 
 
• **Global Reach**:
 
 
• While its headquarters are in **Australia**, the **IEP** maintains several satellite offices in **New York**, **Mexico City**, **Brussels**, and **The Hague** to coordinate with international bodies like the **United Nations** and the **OECD**.
